metadata.question: Was the land surface temperature in Palm Springs, California higher on July 15-21, 2017 than the 2001-2010 average for the same period?

data.raw_code: The user asks: "Was the land surface temperature in Palm Springs, California higher on July 15-21, 2017 than the 2001-2010 average for the same period?" I need to: 1. Get land surface temperature (LST) data for Palm Springs, California. 2. Compare LST for July 15-21, 2017 vs the 2001-2010 average for the same period each year. 3. Use MODIS LST data (MOD11A2 or MYD11A2) which provides 8-day composites. 4. Since July 15-21 is a 7-day period, I need to check which 8-day composite covers it. MODIS 8-day composites: - Day of year 193-200 (July 12-19) - Day of year 201-208 (July 20-27) So July 15-21 spans two composites: partly in DOY 193-200 and partly in 201-208. I could use both composites and average them. 5. Location: Palm Springs, CA coordinates approximately (-116.5453, 33.8303). I'll use a point buffer. 6. For LST, I need to: - Use MODIS Terra MOD11A2.061 (2000-present) or Aqua MYD11A2.061 (2002-present) - Use 'LST_Day_1km' band, scale by 0.02 to get Kelvin, then convert to Celsius if needed - Apply quality mask using 'QC_Day' band 7. Strategy: - Get 2017 data: Filter July 15-21, 2017, get mean LST - Get 2001-2010 data: For each year, get July 15-21 mean LST, then average across years - Compare: Is 2017 LST > 2001-2010 average? 8. Check data availability: MOD11A2 starts 2000, so 2001-2010 should be covered. 9. Potential issues: Cloudy pixels masked out, leading to no valid pixels (C2). Also, need to handle no data (C1) if MODIS has gaps. 10. I'll use a point geometry with 1km buffer to match MODIS resolution. 11. Scale: Use 1000m for reduceRegion. 12. Output: Print intermediate stats (image counts, valid pixel counts, mean LST values). 13. Final answer: A (Yes) if 2017 > average, B (No) if not, or C1/C2/C3/D if issues. But note: The 8-day composite may not align exactly with July 15-21. I need to get the composite that includes these dates. Let's define: - Start date: July 15 - End date: July 22 (exclusive) - For MODIS 8-day, I'll filter by date range and take the mean of available images in that range. Alternatively, I could use daily MODIS LST (MOD11A1) but that's daily and may have more gaps. MOD11A2 is 8-day, so likely one image per period. But July 15-21 spans 7 days, so it may cover parts of two 8-day composites. I'll filter the collection for the date range and compute the mean of the images in that range. Let's plan: Collection: MODIS/006/MOD11A2 (Terra) from 2000-03-05 to present. Band: 'LST_Day_1km' (Kelvin * 0.02) QC: 'QC_Day' for quality mask. Steps: 1. Define geometry (Palm Springs point, buffer 1km). 2. Define date ranges: - 2017: '2017-07-15' to '2017-07-22' - For each year 2001-2010: same month/day range. 3. For each period, filter collection, apply quality mask, compute mean LST over the region and time. 4. For 2001-2010, compute yearly means, then average them. 5. Compare 2017 mean vs 2001-2010 average. Data checks: - If collection size is 0, try MODIS Aqua (MYD11A2) which starts 2002. But for 2001, we need Terra. So if Terra has no data for 2001, we might have to adjust years or output C1. - After masking, check valid pixel count. Logic to distinguish valid zero from null: - If mean LST is not null and within valid range (say 0-60°C for realistic land surface temperature, but in Kelvin ~273-350K), then proceed. - If result is null/NaN, output C3. Let's code accordingly. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions var palmSprings = ee.Geometry.Point(-116.5453, 33.8303).buffer(1000); // 1km buffer var startDate2017 = '2017-07-15'; var endDate2017 = '2017-07-22'; // exclusive var startYear = 2001; var endYear = 2010; // 2. Data Acquisition var modisCol = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/006/MOD11A2') .select(['LST_Day_1km', 'QC_Day']); // Function to apply quality mask function applyQAMask(image) { var qa = image.select('QC_Day'); // Bits 0-1: Mandatory QA flags (0=good, 1=other quality) var mask = qa.bitwiseAnd(3).eq(0); // Keep only good quality return image.updateMask(mask); } // Function to get mean LST for a given date range function getMeanLST(start, end) { var col = modisCol.filterDate(start, end) .filterBounds(palmSprings) .map(applyQAMask); var count = col.size(); // If no images, return null if (count.getInfo() === 0) { return {mean: null, pixelCount: 0, imgCount: 0}; } // Compute mean image over the period var meanImg = col.mean(); // Convert LST from Kelvin*0.02 to Celsius var lstC = meanImg.select('LST_Day_1km').multiply(0.02).subtract(273.15); // Get pixel count and mean value var stats = lstC.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean().combine({ reducer2: ee.Reducer.count(), sharedInputs: true }), geometry: palmSprings, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9, }); var meanVal = stats.get('LST_Day_1km_mean'); var pixelCount = stats.get('LST_Day_1km_count'); return {mean: meanVal, pixelCount: pixelCount, imgCount: count}; } // 3. Get 2017 data var lst2017 = getMeanLST(startDate2017, endDate2017); var imgCount2017 = lst2017.imgCount; var pixelCount2017 = lst2017.pixelCount; var mean2017 = lst2017.mean; // Check for no data or no valid pixels if (imgCount2017.getInfo() === 0) { console.log('2017 Images: 0'); console.log('C1'); return; } if (pixelCount2017.getInfo() === 0) { console.log('2017 Images: ' + imgCount2017.getInfo() + ' (Val: 0 pixels)'); console.log('C2'); return; } // 4. Get 2001-2010 yearly means var yearlyMeans = []; var yearlyCounts = []; for (var year = startYear; year <= endYear; year++) { var start = year + '-07-15'; var end = year + '-07-22'; var lstYear = getMeanLST(start, end); var imgCount = lstYear.imgCount; var pixelCount = lstYear.pixelCount; var meanVal = lstYear.mean; yearlyCounts.push(imgCount); if (imgCount.getInfo() === 0) { console.log(year + ' Images: 0'); console.log('C1'); return; } if (pixelCount.getInfo() === 0) { console.log(year + ' Images: ' + imgCount.getInfo() + ' (Val: 0 pixels)'); console.log('C2'); return; } yearlyMeans.push(meanVal); } // Compute average of yearly means var avgHist = ee.List(yearlyMeans).reduce(ee.Reducer.mean()); // 5. Get values var mean2017Val = mean2017.getInfo(); var avgHistVal = avgHist.getInfo(); // 6. Validation if (mean2017Val === null || avgHistVal === null || isNaN(mean2017Val) || isNaN(avgHistVal)) { console.log('2017 Mean: ' + mean2017Val + ', Historical Avg: ' + avgHistVal); console.log('C3'); return; } // Check for unrealistic values (outside typical LST range for desert in July) // Palm Springs July average high ~42°C, but LST can be higher. Let's set bounds -20 to 80°C. if (mean2017Val < -20 || mean2017Val > 80 || avgHistVal < -20 || avgHistVal > 80) { console.log('2017 Mean: ' + mean2017Val.toFixed(2) + '°C, Historical Avg: ' + avgHistVal.toFixed(2) + '°C'); console.log('C3'); return; } // 7. Output stats and answer console.log('2017 Images: ' + imgCount2017.getInfo() + ' (Val: ' + pixelCount2017.getInfo() + ' pixels)'); console.log('2001-2010 Images per year: ' + yearlyCounts.map(c => c.getInfo()).join(',')); console.log('2017 Mean LST: ' + mean2017Val.toFixed(2) + '°C'); console.log('2001-2010 Avg LST: ' + avgHistVal.toFixed(2) + '°C'); if (mean2017Val > avgHistVal) { console.log('A'); } else { console.log('B'); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
